text:
Nina: FYI saw a sustained tail latency bump starting ~08:12 UTC after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak. p99 went from ~410ms to ~1.2s on the small-GPU pools.
Sam: ack, do you have a perf trace or span link? :eyes: 
Nina: attaching short run from prod profiler. looks like frequent kernel fallback + KV cache evictions when microbatch size climbs above 6.
Mike: can you paste the kernel-selector logs? wondering if we're choosing a fused kernel that degrades for microbatches.
Nina: here's the relevant snippet from logs: 
```
[08:11:58] kernel_selector: model=redwood-3b, seq_len=256, avg_tokens=18
[08:11:58] kernel_selector: picked=fused_att_fast (warmup)
[08:12:01] kernel_selector: picked=fused_att_safe for microbatch=7 (fallback path)
[08:12:02] kv_cache: evict_rate=0.37, evict_ms=12.4
[08:12:03] admission: microbatch_size=7 admitted=18 queued=3
[08:12:04] latency_p99=1230ms
```
Sam: that fallback line is suspicious. fused_att_fast likely has an optimistic path for small batch counts, but our admission controller appears to be creating borderline microbatches (6->7) and tripping a different codepath.
Elaine: also note noisy neighbor on node gpu-14 around same time, tenant=tf-serving had a background large-batch job (OOM-retry loop). Might explain KV thrash.
Karim: reproduced in staging with a workload script: 
```
# repro
python tools/loadtest.py --model redwood-3b --seq-len 256 --qps 180 --concurrency 32 --target-microbatch 7
```
Mike: I ran that, captured perf counters. kernel cycles jumped, L2 cache misses spiked when microbatch crossed 6 -> eviction ratio doubled.
Nina: quick profiler flame (summary):
- fused_att_fast: avg 42ms/token, but tail-heavy when fallback engaged
- fused_att_safe: avg 110ms/token, stable
- KV lookup latency median 1.7ms -> p99 18ms during thrash
Sam: hypothesis: kernel_selector heuristics assume steady-state batch distribution; admission controller's microbatch sizing causes frequent near-threshold choices, flipping kernels and invalidating KV cache locality.
Elaine: proposed mitigation: tweak admission controller to prefer stable microbatch caps (floor to 6 instead of allowing 7) OR adjust selector to prefer safe kernel if microbatch variance > 0.2.
Karim: quick experiment: set admission-controller config: `microbatch_min=2, microbatch_max=6, smoothing_alpha=0.6` and run for 15m. results: p99 reduced to ~480ms, eviction_rate dropped to 0.08.
Mike: if we do controller change we should also add selector hysteresis: don't switch kernel unless roll_avg(tokens_per_batch) crosses threshold for > 5s. avoids flipflop.
Nina: agreed. action items: 
- Sam: add selector hysteresis PR (small change)
- Karen: (ops) patch admission config on canary pool to max=6 for 2h and monitor.
- Mike: add perf counters to heatmap to catch early KV eviction spikes.
Sam: filing follow-up ticket with logs + staging repro: https://internal/issue/INF-2931
deploy-bot: deploy redwood-runtime@canary -> pool-small-gpu scheduled 2026-03-18T09:05:00Z :rocket:
Elaine: monitoring looks good so far after canary patch, p95 improved and queues stabilized. :thumbsup:
Nina: nice. we'll keep this in short postmortem once ops run completes. thanks all.
